abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) progression is driven by complex cellular interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME), where endothelial cell (EC)-tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) crosstalk significantly influences angiogenesis and immune modulation, although the specific subsets and consequences remain unclear. Here, we integrated four single-cell RNA sequencing datasets (50 PDAC; 21 normal adjacent tissues) to profile EC and macrophage subpopulations, subsequently employing CellChat to decipher intercellular communication networks and identify altered ligand-receptor interactions in PDAC. Correlation and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses (TCGA-PAAD) assessed associations and prognostic value, while functional validation used EdU, CCK-8, and Transwell assays on PDAC cells. We identified a distinct endothelial subset (EC0) and macrophage subset (Mac2) with enhanced interaction signals in PDAC. This EC0-Mac2 crosstalk correlated with significant S100A6 upregulation, which was associated with poor patient prognosis. Exogenous S100A6 treatment markedly enhanced PDAC cell proliferation and migration in vitro. In conclusion, EC-Mac crosstalk may promote PDAC progression via S100A6, and this interaction pattern warrants further investigation as a candidate prognostic biomarker and potential target for disrupting stromal communication.
